title: When The Righteous Judge Of Dharma Begins
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: This shabad opens with when the Righteous Judge of Dharma begins to destroy someone, no one can place any obstacle in His Way. It turns the heart toward o Nanak, those who join the Saadh Sangat and meditate on the Lord are saved.
whyItMatters: It matters when life feels alone, unseen, and disconnected because the shabad keeps loneliness inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private momentum.
takeaway: Keep returning to this turn: O Nanak, those who join the Saadh Sangat and meditate on the Lord are saved.

lines.gurmukhi: ਢਾਹਨ ਲਾਗੇ ਧਰਮ ਰਾਇ ਕਿਨਹਿ ਨ ਘਾਲਿਓ ਬੰਧ ॥
lines.transliteration: ddaahan laage dharam rai kineh na ghaalio ba(n)dh ||
lines.translation: When the Righteous Judge of Dharma begins to destroy someone, no one can place any obstacle in His Way.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਉਬਰੇ ਜਪਿ ਹਰੀ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਸਨਬੰਧ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak ubare jap haree saadhasa(n)g sanaba(n)dh ||1||
lines.translation: O Nanak, those who join the Saadh Sangat and meditate on the Lord are saved. ||1||

structure: It opens by naming the condition without ornament: when the Righteous Judge of Dharma begins to destroy someone, no one can place any obstacle in His Way.
The middle movement widens the correction through o Nanak, those who join the Saadh Sangat and meditate on the Lord are saved.
It closes with a return you can actually keep: o Nanak, those who join the Saadh Sangat and meditate on the Lord are saved.
